newsitem.title: UK: U.S. water act favourable for utility credits - S&P.
newsitem.headline: U.S. water act favourable for utility credits - S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday that it expected the recently reauthorised Safe Drinking Water Act in the U.S. to have a favorable, long-term credit impact on water utilities.

"Investor-owned and municipal utilities should view this legislation positively, since it will moderate future compliance obligations, yet maintain high-quality environmental standards and provide some federal funding assistance," S&P associate director Alberto J. Santos said in a report.
S&P said the act marked the beginning of a more common sense approach to testing and monitoring of contaminants.
"In addition, it is a formal adoption of cost/benefit and relative risk analysis in setting maximum contaminant levels for substances that are considered harmful to the general public."

The new act was also the first drinking water legislation to form a state revolving fund programme, which would assist small water systems in meeting regulatory compliance and conducting other drinking water projects, S&P said.

"But the modest $7.6 billion eight-year fund is not nearly enough to help small private and municipal water systems in financing the total cost of complying with water quality standards and upgrade deteriorating water infrastructure."

Given the limited financial and technical resources typically found in small private and municipal water systems, investor-owned utilities were uniquely positioned to help these systems meet existing and future compliance, the agency said.

"In turn, by leveraging their technical personnel and laboratory facilities to assist small water systems, investor-owned utilities will benefit from revenue growth needed to offset low customer growth," the report said.
